what: SAUDI LEGAL FORESIGHT. Current pressure, the legal frontier, and where AI would land if it arrived in the observed forum.

threeKindsOfStatement.OBSERVED: measured in this corpus or quoted from an enacted text this repository holds
threeKindsOfStatement.EXPECTED: follows from an OBSERVED fact plus a stated legal or institutional mechanism

part3_currentOfficialSignalPass.boundedBy: official state sources only; stopped once a high-value current set existed. No news archive, no historical completion.

items.title: 2026 designated the Year of Artificial Intelligence; SDAIA issues guidelines to unify national effort
items.observable_evidence: an official state announcement; no corpus observable follows from it directly
items.possible_legal_consequence: increased institutional AI adoption across government, including justice bodies

items.title: SDAIA opens public consultation on a draft Responsible AI policy via the Istitlaa platform
items.observable_evidence: a named draft instrument under official consultation
items.possible_legal_consequence: a binding or advisory AI policy instrument; if binding and breached, a regulatory rather than commercial forum would see it first

items.title: SDAIA issues rules governing personal data protection licensing and accreditation
items.observable_evidence: a licensing regime around the Personal Data Protection Law
items.possible_legal_consequence: a compliance market and an enforcement channel; disputes would surface in a regulatory forum before a commercial one

items.title: Personal Data Protection Law committees to impose penalties on confirmed violations
items.possible_legal_consequence: the first data-protection disputes with a decided record; NOT in this corpus, whose forum is commercial adjudication

items.title: Law permitting non-Saudi ownership of real estate enters into force 22 January 2026
items.observable_evidence: an instrument in force with a stated date
items.possible_legal_consequence: new transaction volume, and eventually new dispute families; whether any of it reaches published commercial adjudication is unknown

items.title: Labour Law amendments: 38 articles revised, 7 omitted, 2 added
items.institution: Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development
items.observable_evidence: an amendment package in force; the Labour Law is cited only 12 times in this corpus, so its visibility here is minimal
items.possible_legal_consequence: labour disputes are not the commercial forum's docket; observable uptake here is unlikely

items.title: New Enforcement Law welcomed by the Minister of Justice
items.observable_evidence: already carried as LSIG-0004 in the legal signal registry
items.possible_legal_consequence: enforcement output is not published as reasoned judgments, so this corpus cannot observe its uptake

part8_firstCaseReadiness.what: FIRST-AI-CASE READINESS. The capture schema is defined BEFORE the first validated AI-material dispute appears, so the first one is recorded against a fixed template rather than described after the fact.
part8_firstCaseReadiness.trigger: a judgment in this corpus in which an AI system is material to the dispute, not merely mentioned. Materiality is decided by the AI radar's existing L3 rule, which currently returns zero.
capture_fields: ai_issue_family (from the emerging AI law map)
new_doctrinal_source (identity not previously in the canon)
forbidden: inferring AI involvement from writing style
treating a mention of AI as an AI-material dispute
predicting the outcome of the case
naming a judge, a party or a firm
part8_firstCaseReadiness.baseline_at_definition: zero AI-material disputes in the observed corpus. The schema is armed against a base rate of zero, which is the point.

part10_aiComponents.noSingleScore: no AI readiness index is computed. A single number would hide which component moved, and we do not yet know which components matter.

litigation_observability.evidence: no AI-material dispute in the corpus

court_data_observability.evidence: the latest mature quarter is roughly two years behind the session clock and no publication date exists per judgment

part20_frontier.notForecast: the frontier says where change is most likely to originate. It does not forecast any item.
part20_frontier.honestSummary: the two most active current frontiers -- AI governance and data protection -- are the two least observable in this corpus, because their forum is regulatory rather than commercial adjudication.

part22_surpriseReadiness.what: UNKNOWN-UNKNOWN WATCH. The project must be able to discover a future it did not name.
part22_surpriseReadiness.rule: any recurring legal concept, statutory instrument or non-statutory identity that is NOT in a known family and that crosses the support threshold used elsewhere in this repository -- observed in at least ten judgments, in at least two mature quarters -- opens a SURPRISE_LEDGER entry.
appliesTo: instrument track ids not previously court-cited
canonical non-statutory identities outside the 28-identity canon, which currently surface as RAW strings
authority-adjacent formula classes not in the mechanical taxonomy
part22_surpriseReadiness.discipline: the entry is opened FIRST and the explanation is searched for afterwards. An entry with no explanation stays UNKNOWN, and resemblance to an expectation is never evidence.

part23_liveChain.what: LIVE LEGAL CHANGE CHAIN. From this commit onward, an event captured PROSPECTIVELY records milestones as they occur.
part23_liveChain.orderingIsNotRequired: the milestones are stored, not sequenced. The transition programme already showed that an apparent ordering can be an artefact of when the clock was started.
part23_liveChain.captureClass: computed from recorded_at against the event's observable_from, never declared. An event recorded after its observable_from is BACKFILLED and can never be reported as foresight.
part23_liveChain.why: every event this repository holds was recorded after the fact. The chain starts empty on purpose, and that is the point of defining it now.

part16_aiBaseline.reading: Saudi law already permits AI in the procedures of the very forum this corpus observes, while the corpus contains no dispute in which AI is material. Permission is present; consequence is untested.

standingLimitations: the forum. This corpus is published Ministry of Justice commercial adjudication. The two most active current AI frontiers -- AI governance and data protection -- are regulatory, so their first disputes will not appear here.
the observation lag. The latest mature quarter is roughly two years behind the session clock.
nothing in the anchor map asserts that an instrument applies. It records where the system would have to absorb a problem, quoted from the text.
no probability is attached to any branch, horizon or hypothesis.
